# HeartRateLab: Complete Pipeline Demonstration

This notebook demonstrates the complete HeartRateLab pipeline end-to-end:
1. **Load real HRV data**
2. **Fit mechanistic models with Bayesian inference**
3. **Generate synthetic ensemble**
4. **Visualize uncertainty and dynamics**
5. **Validate statistical fit**

## Setup

```{julia}

using Plots, StatsPlots
using Statistics, Random
using DataFrames

# Set random seed for reproducibility
Random.seed!(42)
```

## Part 4: Model Fitting and Synthetic Generation

### 4.1 The Leaky Integrate-and-Fire (LIF) Cardiac Pacemaker

The **Leaky Integrate-and-Fire (LIF)** model represents the sinoatrial node as a single-compartment
membrane whose voltage $V$ is governed by:

$$\tau \frac{dV}{dt} = -(V - V_\text{rest}) + R \cdot I$$

When $V$ crosses the firing threshold $V_\text{threshold}$, a **spike** (heartbeat) is emitted and
$V$ resets to $V_\text{reset}$. The inter-beat interval (IBI) is the time between consecutive
spikes. DifferentialEquations.jl is used to integrate this ODE with `Tsit5()` and a
`ContinuousCallback` for precise spike detection.

| Parameter | Symbol | Value | Physiological meaning |
|-----------|--------|-------|-----------------------|
| Time constant | $\tau$ | 200 ms | Membrane integration timescale |
| Resting potential | $V_\text{rest}$ | −65 mV | Baseline membrane voltage |
| Reset potential | $V_\text{reset}$ | −65 mV | Voltage after spike |
| Spike threshold | $V_\text{thr}$ | −60 mV | Threshold that triggers a beat |
| Membrane resistance | $R$ | 10 MΩ | Input-current scaling |
| **Input current** | **$I$** | **≈ 1.52, fitted** | **Sole free parameter — encodes heart rate** |

The **nullcline** (steady-state without spikes) satisfies $V^* = V_\text{rest} + R \cdot I$.
For $I = 1.52$ we get $V^* \approx -49.8\,\text{mV}$, which lies **above** $V_\text{threshold}$,
guaranteeing periodic spiking — the necessary condition for a functional pacemaker.

```{julia}
# ── Fixed LIF physiological parameters ──────────────────────────────────────
τ_lif       = 200.0   # ms
V_rest_lif  = -65.0   # mV
V_thr_lif   = -60.0   # mV
V_reset_lif = -65.0   # mV
R_lif       = 10.0    # MΩ
I_normal    = 1.52    # dimensionless; typical resting drive

# ── Slope-field grid in (t, V) space ────────────────────────────────────────
V_grid_vals = range(-67.5, -49.5, length = 12)
t_grid_vals = range(0.0, 110.0,  length = 12)

T_flat    = vec([t for t in t_grid_vals, v in V_grid_vals])
V_flat    = vec([v for t in t_grid_vals, v in V_grid_vals])
dVdt_flat = vec([(-(v - V_rest_lif) + R_lif * I_normal) / τ_lif
                  for t in t_grid_vals, v in V_grid_vals])

# Normalise arrows so all have the same visual length
arrow_scale = 5.0
norms       = sqrt.(1.0 .+ dVdt_flat .^ 2)
dT_arrows   =  arrow_scale ./ norms
dV_arrows   = (dVdt_flat .* arrow_scale) ./ norms

p_field = quiver(T_flat, V_flat,
    quiver  = (dT_arrows, dV_arrows),
    xlabel  = "Time (ms, model units)",
    ylabel  = "Membrane Voltage V (mV)",
    title   = "LIF Slope Field  (I = $(I_normal))",
    color   = :steelblue, alpha = 0.7, linewidth = 1.5,
    xlims   = (0, 120), ylims = (-69, -48),
    legend  = :bottomright, label = "")

hline!([V_rest_lif]; linestyle = :dash, color = :gray,   lw = 2,
       label = "V_rest = $(V_rest_lif) mV")
hline!([V_thr_lif];  linestyle = :dash, color = :crimson, lw = 2,
       label = "V_threshold = $(V_thr_lif) mV")
display(p_field)
```

### 4.2 Simulated Voltage Trace

A direct DifferentialEquations.jl simulation reveals the sub-threshold charging and resets.
With `I = 1.52` the model period is ≈ 80 ms (model time), which maps to ≈ 800 ms
(physiological time) after the ×10 scaling applied in `simulate()`.

```{julia}
using DifferentialEquations

# ODE right-hand side
function lif_ode!(du, u, p, t)
    V = u[1]
    τ_p, V_rest_p, R_p, I_p = p
    du[1] = (-(V - V_rest_p) + R_p * I_p) / τ_p
end

# Spike-detection callback (upward threshold crossing)
spike_times_trace = Float64[]
spike_cond(u, t, integrator)  = u[1] - V_thr_lif
function spike_affect!(integrator)
    push!(spike_times_trace, integrator.t)
    integrator.u[1] = V_reset_lif
    length(spike_times_trace) >= 10 && terminate!(integrator)
end
cb = ContinuousCallback(spike_cond, spike_affect!, nothing,
                        rootfind = SciMLBase.RightRootFind)

prob = ODEProblem(lif_ode!, [V_rest_lif],
                 (0.0, 1200.0),
                 [τ_lif, V_rest_lif, R_lif, I_normal])
sol  = solve(prob, Tsit5(); callback = cb, dtmax = 0.1, saveat = 0.2)

p_trace = plot(sol.t, sol[1, :];
    xlabel = "Time (ms, model units)",
    ylabel = "Membrane Voltage (mV)",
    title  = "LIF Voltage Trace — I = $(I_normal)",
    color  = :steelblue, lw = 2, label = "V(t)")
hline!([V_thr_lif];  linestyle = :dash, color = :crimson, lw = 1.5,
       label = "V_threshold = $(V_thr_lif) mV")
hline!([V_rest_lif]; linestyle = :dash, color = :gray,   lw = 1.5,
       label = "V_rest = $(V_rest_lif) mV")

if length(spike_times_trace) >= 2
    ibis_model = diff(spike_times_trace)
    mean_T_model = round(mean(ibis_model); digits = 1)
    println("Spikes detected : $(length(spike_times_trace))")
    println("Mean model IBI  : $(mean_T_model) ms  →  physiological IBI ≈ $(round(mean_T_model * 10; digits=1)) ms")
    for st in spike_times_trace
        vline!([st]; linestyle = :dot, color = :orange, alpha = 0.8, label = "")
    end
end

# ── Bottom panel: IBIs on the ×10 physiological timeline ────────────────────
# Each IBI is plotted at the midpoint between its two bounding spikes,
# rescaled to physiological time (model time × 10).
p_ibi = plot(; xlabel = "Time (ms, physiological)",
               ylabel = "IBI (ms)",
               title  = "Model IBIs — physiological timeline (×10 rescaling)",
               ylims  = (0, nothing), legend = :topright)

if length(spike_times_trace) >= 2
    ibis_model   = diff(spike_times_trace)
    # Midpoint of each inter-spike interval, scaled to physiological time
    t_ibi_phys   = (spike_times_trace[1:end-1] .+ spike_times_trace[2:end]) ./ 2 .* 10
    ibis_phys    = ibis_model .* 10

    # Stem-style: vertical lines from zero up to each IBI value
    for (t_i, ibi_i) in zip(t_ibi_phys, ibis_phys)
        plot!(p_ibi, [t_i, t_i], [0.0, ibi_i];
              color = :teal, lw = 2, label = "")
    end
    scatter!(p_ibi, t_ibi_phys, ibis_phys;
             color = :teal, markersize = 6, label = "IBI (model × 10)")

    mean_ibi_phys = round(mean(ibis_phys); digits = 1)
    hline!(p_ibi, [mean_ibi_phys];
           linestyle = :dash, color = :orange, lw = 1.5,
           label = "Mean IBI = $(mean_ibi_phys) ms")
    xlims!(p_ibi, (0, t_ibi_phys[end] + 100))
end

plot(p_trace, p_ibi; layout = (2, 1), size = (800, 600))
```

### 4.3 Rolling-Window Estimation of Input Current I(t)

We treat $I$ as **slowly varying** over the recording and estimate it on short, overlapping
windows of heartbeats. This converts the scalar fit into a time series $\hat{I}(t)$, making
visible how the autonomic drive to the heart changes over time.

**Window parameters**: 10-beat window · 2-beat stride.

#### Method speed comparison (single window)

```{julia}
window_size = 10
stride      = 2
window1     = real_data[1:window_size]
lif_base    = LIF()

println("Fitting single window of $(window_size) beats with both methods…\n")

t_grad  = @elapsed result_grad  = fit(lif_base, window1; method = :gradient)
println("  :gradient  →  $(round(t_grad; digits = 3)) s   I = $(round(result_grad.params.I; digits = 6))")
println("  Converged : $(result_grad.diagnostics["converged"])  |  Iterations: $(result_grad.diagnostics["iterations"])")
println()

t_bayes = @elapsed result_bayes = fit(lif_base, window1;
    method = :bayesian, chains = 1, samples = 200)
println("  :bayesian  →  $(round(t_bayes; digits = 2)) s   I ≈ $(round(result_bayes.params.I; digits = 6))")
println()

faster = t_grad < t_bayes ? ":gradient" : ":bayesian"
println("▶ Faster method: $(faster) — will be used for the rolling fit")
```

#### Rolling fit over full recording

```{julia}
n_beats       = length(real_data)
window_starts = collect(1:stride:(n_beats - window_size + 1))
t_cumsum_ms   = cumsum(real_data)          # absolute beat timestamps in ms

I_series = Vector{Float64}(undef, length(window_starts))
t_series  = Vector{Float64}(undef, length(window_starts))

println("Fitting $(length(window_starts)) windows (size=$(window_size), stride=$(stride))…")
for (k, s) in enumerate(window_starts)
    w         = real_data[s : s + window_size - 1]
    res       = fit(LIF(), w; method = :gradient)
    I_series[k] = res.params.I
    # Window centre time: midpoint beat timestamp
    center_idx  = s + window_size ÷ 2 - 1
    t_series[k] = t_cumsum_ms[center_idx]
end
println("Done — $(length(I_series)) I estimates computed.")

t_sec = t_series ./ 1000.0          # convert ms → s for the x-axis

p_I = plot(t_sec, I_series;
    xlabel = "Time (s)",
    ylabel = "Estimated Input Current I",
    title  = "Continuous LIF Drive  I(t)  (window=$(window_size) beats · stride=$(stride))",
    lw = 1.5, color = :teal, label = "Î(t)")
hline!([1.52]; linestyle = :dash, color = :gray, lw = 1.5,
       label = "Default I = 1.52")
display(p_I)

println("\nI(t) summary:")
println("  Mean  : $(round(mean(I_series);    digits = 6))")
println("  Std   : $(round(std(I_series);     digits = 6))")
println("  Min   : $(round(minimum(I_series); digits = 6))")
println("  Max   : $(round(maximum(I_series); digits = 6))")
```

## References

Key publications on HRV analysis and mechanistic models:

- **Van der Pol Model**: Lopez-Chamorro et al. (2018). Cardiac Pulse Modeling Using
  Modified van der Pol Oscillator. Bioinformatics and Biomedical Engineering.

- **Bayesian Inference**: Gelman et al. (2013). Bayesian Data Analysis (3rd ed).
  Chapman and Hall.

- **HRV Features**: Task Force of the European Society of Cardiology (1996).
  Heart rate variability: standards of measurement, physiological interpretation
  and clinical use. Circulation 93(5): 1043-1065.

- **Statistical Testing**: Massey (1951). The Kolmogorov-Smirnov test for goodness
  of fit. Journal of the American Statistical Association.
